answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing escrowed jobs for distinct counterparties, with rewards released after both sides post matching receipts. A trellis of cross-checks lets the network spot clusters whose apparent endorsements all trace back to the same accounts; those links count as one, not many. To multiply influence, an attacker must fund real jobs with independent people and risk losing escrow when claims disagree. At the nadir, a pile of freshly minted identities buys no reputation; a walnut-sized budget cannot cheaply fake costly, diverse history.
